key_insight: Deep learning Hessian spectra can be explained as symmetry breaking from a nearby highly symmetric reference model, which naturally produces large zero-like kernels plus clustered eigenvalue outliers.
engineering_relevance: This offers a structural way to interpret sharpness, flat directions, and optimizer behavior across architectures, helping diagnose and compare training landscapes in modern neural networks.
method: Identify a nearby reference configuration with hidden invariances beyond standard weight symmetries.
Analyze the Hessian spectrum under these symmetries to obtain high-multiplicity eigenvalues and large kernels.
Compare with the original model to see how symmetry breaking splits clusters into the observed bulk-and-outlier pattern.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a detailed theoretical analysis of three-layer ReLU networks and extensions to convolutional, graph, transformer, NTK, layerwise Hessians, and the Gauss-Newton matrix, showing the same spectral mechanism across settings.
watch_item: The framework is primarily structural and model-dependent, so the choice of reference configuration or metric may affect how directly the predicted spectral clusters match a given trained network.
paper_title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking
